name: Phlegon of Tralles
summary:
Phlegon of Tralles was a Greek writer and freedman of the emperor Hadrian, who lived in the 2nd century AD.

Born in the late 1st century AD, Phlegon rose to prominence as a poet and historian, serving as the imperial secretary and chief librarian of Hadrian's library at Ephesus. His most notable work is the 'Chronicle', which provided valuable information on ancient Greek history and mythology.

Phlegon's writings played a significant role in shaping our understanding of ancient Greece, particularly in the fields of history, literature, and philosophy. He was also known for his translations of works by famous philosophers such as Plato and Aristotle.

Despite his contributions to classical scholarship, Phlegon remains somewhat of an enigma, with many details about his life and work shrouded in mystery. Nevertheless, his legacy continues to inspire scholars and historians seeking to uncover the secrets of ancient Greece.
